sources.title: Self-pollination in island and mainland populations of the introduced hummingbird-pollinated plant, Nicotiana glauca (Solanaceae)
measured_links: pollen removal and stigma pollen deposition
open intact versus open emasculated reproductive-assurance test

sampling_notes.autogamy: 1998 CAT n=18 plants, SED n=11, STA n=12; 1999 CRU n=9 and STA n=9
sampling_notes.pollen_limitation: 1998 CAT n=24, SED n=11, STA n=12; 1999 CRU n=10, CAT n=17, STA n=13
sampling_notes.emasculation: paired treatments on at least 10 plants at CAT, SED and STA in spring 1998, STA again summer 1998, and CRU summer 1999
sampling_notes.pollen_transfer: at least five flowers per plant on at least six plants per site; CRU and STA in Nov 1999 and CRU, CAT, STA and MON in Jun 2000

source_route.publisher_full_text: Wiley / American Journal of Botany free-access article

source_route.checksum_blocker: Exact Deep Blue PDF bytes were not recovered in the current automated route; keep byte-level source lock pending.

sources.source_native_conclusion: Island populations had higher self-pollination capacity, especially the recently colonized Santa Cruz population, but current island pollinator service was not lower and island plants were not pollen limited; emasculation did not reveal stronger current reproductive-assurance dependence on selfing on islands.

sources.title: Island-mainland difference in Nicotiana glauca (Solanaceae) corolla length: a product of pollinator-mediated selection?
measured_links: phenotypic selection using pollen transfer, fruit set and seed count
single-visit hummingbird pollen deposition and removal at CAT and STA
supplemental hand-pollination control for non-pollinator fecundity effects

source_native_numeric_anchors.island_corolla_difference: approximately 1 mm longer on islands on average
source_native_numeric_anchors.single_visit_design: sets of 20 tagged flowers; repeated for 3 days for two sets at CAT and five at STA; at least six Allen's and three Anna's hummingbirds at CAT and at least two Anna's at STA
source_native_numeric_anchors.per_visit_result: Allen's hummingbirds deposited and removed significantly less pollen per visit than Anna's, but per-visit effectiveness was not associated with corolla length

source_route.publisher_record: Springer Evolutionary Ecology article DOI record

cross_source_linkage.why_partial_not_complete: The two papers share named populations and overlapping study years, and together cover floral response, pollinator effectiveness/service, and reproductive dependency/assurance. However, the current source record does not establish that the floral, per-visit, and reproductive experiments used the same tagged plants or an exact prespecified temporal transfer unit. Numeric effect extraction and byte-level source locking are also incomplete.
cross_source_linkage.allowed_claim: This system supplies a genuine partial mechanistic bridge and, importantly, an alternative-mechanism test: current island pollinator service did not explain the stronger selfing capacity, making colonization/establishment filtering a live mechanism rather than assuming post-establishment pollinator scarcity.
blocked_claims: do not call this a complete causal chain
do not infer historical selection from current contrasts
do not treat self-compatibility alone as effective dependency
do not pool the 2004 and 2007 measurements as if they were the same individual-level observations
do not admit a cross-system effect size until source-native numeric estimates, uncertainty, hierarchy and provenance are locked

next_actions: Recover exact 2004 Table 1/Table 5/Figure 2/Figure 7 numeric values and uncertainty from a stable source artifact without digitizing when machine-readable or tabular values are available.
